title: Duplicated Shared Knowledge across Documentation Files (DRY Violation)
pattern: Identical business rules or policy constraints documented in multiple independent source comments.
why_bad: Dual-maintenance failure. When business fees or rules change, developers must hunt down and update every scattered text reference, guaranteeing stale, conflicting documentation.
detection: Substantially identical descriptions of business formulas or numeric limits appearing in comments in separate source files.
counterexample: Business rules centralized as named constants or a single policy function, referenced by name from any comment that needs them.
fix: Centralize business rules in code as structured constants or unified methods, and reference them by name rather than hardcoding numbers in prose comments.
source: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (1999), Chapter 2 ("Duplication in Documentation").
